_question: How does a segment tree answer a range query in log n time?

beats.line: So the tree stores a range in every node. That is the whole trick.
Right. The root covers the whole array, and each child splits its parent's range in half.
So the leaves end up being single elements, since you keep halving down to size one.
Exactly. And a query walks down asking one question per node: does my range fit entirely inside yours?
Wait, so it does not visit every leaf in the query range one by one?
That is the part everyone gets backwards. It stops early whenever a node fits completely, so it only ever touches about log n of them.
